mcqs.q: Did the Battle of Bosworth in 1485 end the Wars of the Roses?
options: It killed Richard III and put Henry Tudor on the throne, but Yorkist threats (Simnel 1487, Warbeck 1490s) continued — the wars only truly ended with Stoke Field in 1487.
They were a religious war between Catholics and Protestants.
Bosworth in 1485 ended the Wars of the Roses immediately.
Bosworth was a naval battle fought off the south coast of England.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Elizabethan Settlement 1559”?
options: Period of instability: Edward VI's Protestant reforms, Mary I's Catholic restoration, succession disputes, Wyatt's rebellion.
Acts of Supremacy and Uniformity creating moderate Protestant Church; Royal Injunctions enforced Book of Common Prayer.
Henry Tudor defeated Richard III ending Wars of the Roses; legitimised through marriage to Elizabeth of York 1486.
Parliament protested at Elizabeth's grants of trade monopolies; Golden Speech promised reform but issue passed to Stuarts.
